Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romania’s interim foreign minister, Oana Țoiu, announced on Monday, July 20, that the Visa Waiver program remains a priority in Romania's relationship with the United States, but the timing of its acceptance depends on political discussions, reducing the visa refusal rate, and the Trump administration. "Visa Waiver is a priority in the bilateral relationship. As you know, in the relationship between the United States and Romania, we had already managed to reach the threshold of under 3% for visa refusals, a threshold necessary for us to enter the Visa Waiver program," Oana Țoiu said on Monday evening on TVR Info . Romania was formally designated the 43rd country to join the US Visa Waiver Program (VWP) in 2025 by the Biden administration. However, just days before the official entry date, the US announced that it had temporarily suspended the implementation of the Electronic System for Travel Authorization for Romanian citizens. Weeks later, in early May, it officially rescinded Romania's Visa Waiver Program (VWP) designation . In October 2025, Romanian president Nicușor Dan stressed that the move should be seen as a domestic policy signal in the United States, where migration remains a contentious issue. Romania’s Visa Waiver application is currently handled by the Ministry of Internal Affairs. "When it moves forward depends on the political discussion, certainly, on reducing the refusal rate again to that threshold, but also on president Trump's administration in terms of the paradigm it has regarding travel and the opening of the border,” according to the acting foreign minister. She mentioned that the first criterion for resolving the situation is the percentage of visa application refusals. "When we received approval to enter the Visa Waiver program, we met this 3% criterion. Now, because, of course, many people obtained visas during that period and did not renew them because it was not necessary, the number of refusals is higher,” Țoiu said. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Megaflopp|Dreamstime.com ) Read next 01 October 2025 Politics President Dan says Visa Waiver setback driven more by US migration politics than Romania's political situation Normal Politics Romania’s acceptance into Visa Waiver program depends on Trump admin, interim foreign minister says 21 July 2026 Radu Dumitrescu Like this article? https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj9d.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, L-R: Michael McLeod, Alex Formenton, Carter Hart, Dillon Dube and Cal Foote Published 4 hours ago Four ice hockey players who were acquitted of sexual assault last year should remain barred from representing Canada at international level because they broke Hockey Canada's code of conduct, an independent appeals board has ruled. The board recommended that four of the five acquitted players remain suspended from all Hockey Canada-sanctioned programmes. The fifth player, Alex Formenton, was also deemed to have broken conduct rules, but is now being reinstated. The former players for Canada's under-20s junior hockey team were accused of sexual assault over an incident that took place in 2018. They were found not guilty in July 2025. The players are Michael McLeod, Dillon Dube, Cal Foote and Carter Hart, as well as Formenton. The ruling does not change the fact that all five players are eligible to play for teams that compete in the National Hockey League (NHL), which operates separately from Hockey Canada. All five were allowed by the NHL to sign contracts again for the league's teams late last year. The NHL operates under a separate authority to Hockey Canada, and conducted its own investigation into the incident that was at the centre of the legal case. While Forementon is eligible for immediate reinstatement by Hockey Canada, the others will have to wait for months or years before they can return to the ice at an international level. Foote will be eligible on 10 November of this year, while Hart and Dube will be eligible on 10 November 2027 and 10 November 2028 respectively. McLeod will have to wait until 10 November 2030. Officials did not say why the reinstatement dates differed for each player. Five ice hockey players found not guilty in Canada sexual assault case Published 25 July 2025 The players had been accused of assaulting the woman, known as EM, in a hotel room in 2018 in London, Ontario, where they had been attending a gala. They were acquitted in July 2025 when Justice Maria Carroccia said she did not find EM's evidence "credible or reliable". The court heard that the woman had met the players at a bar and later went back to the hotel room to have consensual sex with McLeod. Other players then entered the room and engaged in further sexual acts with her. The central issue of the trial was whether EM, who was 20 at the time of the incident, had consented to every sexual act in the hotel room that night. Lawyers for the players contended that EM asked the men to have sex with her and they believed she gave consent. EM, however, testified that she was intoxicated and felt fearful of the men. While she had initially agreed to have sex with McLeod, she testified that she did not agree to what unfolded afterwards. Despite the fact that the incident happened eight years ago, the case remains on the minds of many in Canada. "This case started a national conversation about safe sport and the problematic culture in men's hockey," said Adam van Koeverden, Canada's current secretary of sport, in a statement after the Wednesday's ruling by the appeals board. "It is the voices of women and survivors, and the courage and bravery it takes to come forward, that have led to changes we are seeing in toxic culture." Van Koeverden said there has been progress at Hockey Canada to "address long-standing systemic failures" and said that national sport organisations must be held accountable. https://business.scoop.co.nz/2026/09/12/.text: Scoop Werewolf Wellington Business Pacific Community Review of Books InfoPages Home Agriculture Finance Transport ICT Economy Manufacturing Energy Policy More Home Agriculture Finance Transport ICT Economy Manufacturing Energy Policy More Scoop Werewolf Wellington Business Pacific Community Review of Books InfoPages Technological Support For A Modern Healthcare Environment Article – Hugh Grant With hospitals experiencing financial pressures, technology needs to leave a beneficial impact that lasts for a long time. Hospitals are expected to provide fast, safe, and reliable care while their staff manage increasingly demanding workloads. Nurses and other healthcare professionals can spend a significant amount of their time moving supplies, medications, and documents around a facility instead of focusing directly on patients. At the same time, hospitals face financial pressure, cybersecurity threats, and the continuing need to provide patients with the best care. These challenges make operational technology an increasingly important part of how modern hospitals function. Healthcare workers are expected to handle a large amount of work on a daily basis. Depending on the country, nurses can be responsible for as many as 11 patients per day. The strain is reflected in the workforce itself, with more than 83% of people in the nursing profession reporting that they feel mentally overwhelmed at work. There is also a projected shortage of more than 4 million nurses worldwide by 2030. When fewer healthcare workers are available to handle a growing workload, hospitals have to find ways to make the time of existing staff count. Technology can ease some of the strain and stress put on hospital staff. Pneumatic tube systems, for example, can move materials through a hospital without needing a staff member to physically carry them between locations. The technology can process more than 10,000 transactions each day, while documents can travel 700% faster than they would with human walkers. Cancer medication that takes 10 minutes to transport manually can take just two minutes using a tube system. The time saved can be built up to allow healthcare workers more time overall to concentrate on patient care. Technology also provides a way to monitor the movement of materials through a hospital. Staff can use a touchscreen interface to manage the system, while RFID technology can track a tube’s location and provide information about when it has arrived. Many hospital pharmacies can transport 90% or more of their materials using a carrier. In Germany alone, approximately 10,000 red blood cell units need to be transported through hospitals each day. Hospitals are not always in good financial standings. In 2024, one in five hospitals was considered at high risk for financial default. Financial difficulties occur in other healthcare systems as well, including public hospitals in Japan, which reported that 90% operated at a deficit in 2024. Victorian public hospitals in Australia were also dealing with deficits exceeding $1 billion, while hospital debt in Hungary reached €300 million in 2024. With hospitals experiencing financial pressures, technology needs to leave a beneficial impact that lasts for a long time. An investment that reduces unnecessary manual work, improves the movement of supplies, or helps staff complete routine tasks more quickly can potentially address several operational problems at once. Where can technology provide the greatest practical benefit? As hospitals become increasingly dependent on technology, worries about cybersecurity have increased. 42% of healthcare-related ransomware attacks in Europe targeted hospitals. This creates a difficult balance for healthcare facilities. Technology can improve the speed and efficiency of hospital operations, but the systems supporting those operations also need their own proper protection. Keeping technology updated and on-premises is one productive way hospitals can help prevent malicious cyberattacks. Patient safety provides another reason to examine hospital workflows. More than 80% of illnesses are transmitted by hands, while high-touch hospital surfaces can carry 18 human pathogens and 60 different kinds of bacteria. Every time staff physically handle materials and move them around a facility, there is another opportunity for human contact to enter the process. Systems that allow materials to be transported without requiring workers to carry them throughout the hospital can help reduce unnecessary handling. Hospitals will continue to struggle with staffing shortages, financial constraints, cybersecurity concerns and demanding patient-care requirements. Technology cannot completely remove those problems on its own, but thoughtfully designed operational systems can help facilities work around some of the pressures. By improving how materials move through a hospital and reducing the mountain of responsibilities put on staff, technology can become an important part of creating a better healthcare environment.
